```{r}
#Directories for each data folder established, static data read in
static_data <- read_parquet("https://intro-datascience.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/SC-data/static_house_info.parquet")
weather_folder <- "https://intro-datascience.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/SC-data/weather/2023-weather-data/"
energy_folder <- "https://intro-datascience.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/SC-data/2023-houseData/"
```

```{r}
weather_summary <- function(county) {
  #Takes the county and weather directory and forms the URL, then reads it in
  weatherURL <- paste0(weather_folder, county, ".csv")
  weatherDF <- read_csv(url(weatherURL))
  
  #Only takes weather data from July
  weatherDF <- weatherDF[months(weatherDF$date_time) %in% month.name[7],]
  return(weatherDF)
}
```

```{r}
merged_row <- function(id) {
  #Takes the static data from just the house selected
  single_house_static_data <- static_data[static_data$bldg_id == id,]
  
  #Gets energy data
  energyDF <- energy_summary(id)
  
  #Selecting static data we want
  newDF <- single_house_static_data %>% select(bldg_id, 
                  in.sqft, 
                  in.geometry_stories,
                  in.bedrooms,
                  in.county,
                  in.weather_file_latitude,
                  in.weather_file_longitude,
                  in.hvac_cooling_efficiency,
                  in.usage_level,
                  in.windows,
                  in.window_areas,
                  in.insulation_ceiling,
                  in.insulation_floor,
                  in.insulation_foundation_wall,
                  in.insulation_rim_joist,
                  in.insulation_roof,
                  in.insulation_slab,
                  in.insulation_wall,
                  in.ducts)
  
  #Gets weather data
  weatherDF <- weather_summary(newDF$in.county)
  
  #Puts static, energy, and weather data into one dataframe
  newDF <- bind_cols(newDF, energyDF, weatherDF)
  
  return(newDF)
}
```

```{r}
#5000 rows is way too many to process and will take too long to run--so we'll do a random sample
#This will be a stratified random sample to make we are as representative of each county as possible
#This will create a merged dataframe

combine_and_sample <- function(static_df, n) {
  #Perform a random stratified sample
  fraction = n / nrow(static_df)
  
  sampled_data = static_df %>% 
    group_by(in.county) %>% 
    sample_frac(fraction)
  
  #Merge sampled rows by building ID
  unique_ids <- unique(sampled_data$bldg_id)
  
  list_of_dfs <- lapply(unique_ids, function(id) {
    message(paste("Processing ID:", id)) 
    return(merged_row(id))
  })
  
  #Combine all individual dataframes into one
  final_df <- bind_rows(list_of_dfs)
  
  return(final_df)
}
```

```{r}
#Let's run the function on a sample of 250 houses
mergedDF <- combine_and_sample(static_data, 250)

#Examines the result
head(mergedDF)
```

#Find NA
check_factor_nas = function(df, col_name) {
  na_count = sum(is.na(df[[col_name]]))
  total = nrow(df)
  pct = round(na_count / total * 100, 2)
  cat(col_name, ": ", na_count, " NAs (", pct, "%)\n", sep = "")
}

```{r}
#There are some values that we don't need to create/use any predictive models
#Things like bldg_id and county (a character value) can't account for energy usage
#Leaving in total usage would make it a predictor for how much is used per sqft which we don't want
modelDF <- mergedDF
modelDF <- modelDF %>% select(-c('bldg_id',
                                 'in.county',
                                 'in.weather_file_latitude',
                                 'in.weather_file_longitude',
                                 'total_usage',
                                 'time',
                                 'in.insulation_rim_joist',
                                 'in.insulation_roof',
                                 'in.insulation_slab'
                              ))
```

```{r}
#Multiple regression model
lmModel <- lm(usage_per_sqft ~ ., data=modelDF)
summary(lmModel)

trainList <- createDataPartition(y=modelDF$usage_per_sqft, p=.60, list=FALSE)
trainSet <- modelDF[trainList,]
testSet <- modelDF[-trainList,]

predDF <- predict(lmModel, testSet)

sqrt(mean((predDF - testSet$usage_per_sqft)^2))
```



```{r}
#New dataset with all July temperatures 5 degrees warmer (in Celsius)
hotter_data <- modelDF
hotter_data$'Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]' <- hotter_data$'Dry Bulb Temperature [°C]' + 5
#We'll need to add time back in from mergedDF
#We might need to separate the hour from everything as well
hotter_data$time <- mergedDF %>% select('time')
summary(hotter_data)
#Apparently str() showed that there was a time value of POSIXct format within
#hotter_data$time, if I didn't call it it wouldn't work otherwise...never seen that before
hotter_data$hour <- hour(hotter_data$time$time)

#Let's predict with this new data using our best model
hotter_data$hotter_usage_pred <- predict(lmModel, newdata=hotter_data)

#We don't need the full time anymore now that we have the hour
hotter_data <- hotter_data %>% select(-c('time'))
```

```{r}
#We'll need to sum up the energy usage per sqft for each house
hourly_usage <- hotter_data %>%
  #Groups by the hour column we just created
  group_by(hour) %>%
  summarise(
    #Sum of current usage per sqft
    current_sum = sum(usage_per_sqft),
    #Sum of predicted future use per sqft
    hotter_sum = sum(hotter_usage_pred)
  )
```

```{r}

  geom_line(aes(y = current_sum, color = "Current Usage Per Square Foot (kWh/sqft)"), linewidth = 1) + 
  geom_line(aes(y = hotter_sum, color = "Future Usage Per Square Foot (kWh/sqft)"), linewidth = 1) + 
  xlab("Hour of Day") +
  ylab("Usage Per Square Foot (KWH/sqft)") +
  ggtitle("Hourly Energy Usage Per Square Foot (in kWh/sqft)") +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Key", values = c("Current Usage Per Square Foot (kWh/sqft)" = "green", 
                                              "Future Usage Per Square Foot (kWh/sqft)" = "red")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#Current peak energy demand
current_peak <- max(hourly_usage$current_sum)

#Future peak energy demand
future_peak <- max(hourly_usage$hotter_sum)

#Calculate percent increase
((future_peak - current_peak) / current_peak) * 100
```

> This is a pretty big increase in demand!!
